react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolite set is dominated by C19/C18 steroid hormones, producing a striking cross-paradigm consensus on the androgen-and-estrogen axis. RaMP multi-database ORA identifies KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis) and SMPDB:SMP00068 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) as the top hits, both with FDR 2.16×10⁻¹⁴ and fold enrichment ~1250, driven by five input steroids: dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA, C01227), androstenedione (C00280), testosterone (C00535), estradiol (C00951), and dihydrotestosterone (C03917). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently recovers hsa00140 as its top result, confirming the same five-hit roster. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis strengthens this finding: the top MUMM pathway 'C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism' achieves p=0.00227 with an all-10-compound overlap, and the closely related 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' follows at p=0.00378 with 9/9 input steroids matched, giving the highest per-pathway coverage of any tool. A secondary m/z-direct signal hits the prostaglandin axis (MUMM rank 2, p=0.0196) through thromboxane A₂ (C02198), consistent with arachidonic acid cascade activation. Dehydroascorbic acid (C05422) registers on the ascorbate-utilization network (MUMM rank 3, p=0.0413) as a lower-confidence peripheral hit. Quinolinic acid (C03722) appears in both the tryptophan and nicotinamide vitamin-B3 branches (MUMM rank 4-9), suggesting a secondary perturbation of NAD⁺-precursor metabolism. The dobutamine (C06967) and 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutaric acid (C01127) signals do not reach enrichment significance across any tool, indicating they may be context-specific or pharmacological outliers.
